questions: Which HTTP methods are accepted at each generated-description path, and what must happen for HEAD, OPTIONS and other methods?
Which HTTP method or methods are accepted at each documentation path, and therefore which requests to those paths receive 405?

quotes:
The framework also serves its generated description of the four routes at
`/docs`, `/redoc` and `/openapi.json` without a token; it names the routes and the forms of their bodies and
answers, and holds no credential, server path or project data.

A path that is not a route answers 404, and a route's path with another method answers 405, both with the
framework's own body and not M08.
judgement.divergence: One implementation accepts HEAD at `/openapi.json` and returns the generated-description headers without a body; another registers only GET and returns 405, which the HTTP caller notices.
judgement.why: The documentation paths are fixed but their accepted methods are not, so the router's observable input and error behaviour remains open.

quotes:
The framework also serves its generated description of the four routes at
`/docs`, `/redoc` and `/openapi.json` without a token; it names the routes and the forms of their bodies and
answers, and holds no credential, server path or project data.

1. Every operation except the health answer requires exactly one `Authorization` field. Its value is
   the scheme `Bearer`, compared without regard to case as HTTP defines an authentication scheme, one
   space and the token, compared whole, case-sensitively and in constant time. A request without that
   field, with more than one, or with any other value is refused with the UNAUTHORIZED member of
   = models.RefusalCode before its identifiers or body are examined.
judgement.why: The new State 5 passage permits unauthenticated documentation operations while A5 rule 1 makes the health answer the sole unauthenticated operation.
